# Peptide Chooser

> An independent US comparison site: peptide products next to FDA-approved alternatives, with evidence, FDA status and price per month for each goal. We compare; we never sell.


## Home and goals (8 pages)

- [Best peptides by goal, compared | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/): Find the right option for your goal and where to get it at the best price. FDA-approved options first, research-use peptides with their real status.
- [Peptides for hair loss vs proven options | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/hair/): Peptides for hair loss next to finasteride and minoxidil: FDA status, evidence in people and price per month for each option, checked and dated.
- [Peptides for skin vs proven options | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/skin/): Copper peptides, Matrixyl and Argireline next to tretinoin, the cream the FDA approved for wrinkles. What each does, how you get it, what it costs.
- [Weight loss peptides vs Wegovy, Zepbound | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/weight-loss/): Wegovy and Zepbound are FDA approved for weight loss; compounded copies and retatrutide are not. Online clinic prices compared, with any FDA letter shown.
- [Muscle growth peptides vs what is approved | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/muscle/): CJC-1295, ipamorelin, sermorelin and tesamorelin for muscle and growth hormone: what each is, what is approved and for what, and what sellers charge.
- [BPC-157 and TB-500 for healing, compared | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/recovery/): BPC-157 and TB-500 are sold for injuries and joints, but neither is approved for any use. The evidence, the FDA's July 2026 proposal and what sellers charge.
- [PT-141 and peptides for sex drive compared | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/libido/): Bremelanotide (Vyleesi) is FDA approved for low sexual desire in women. The same molecule is sold as PT-141 without approval. What that means, and the prices.
- [Peptides for energy and aging, compared | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/longevity/): Epitalon, MOTS-c and NAD+ shots are sold for energy and anti-aging. None is FDA approved; the FDA reviewed two in July 2026. The evidence and the prices.

- [Is BPC-157 legal in the US? What the FDA decided](https://peptidechooser.com/learn/is-bpc-157-legal/): BPC-157 is not FDA approved. What the July 2026 FDA review proposed, what research-use labels mean and how we check the shops that sell it.

- [How to read a peptide COA (certificate of analysis)](https://peptidechooser.com/learn/how-to-read-a-coa/): What a peptide certificate of analysis tests (purity, identity, amount, endotoxin, sterility), who issues it, and why it only covers one batch.

- [What an FDA warning letter means for a seller](https://peptidechooser.com/learn/what-an-fda-warning-letter-means/): An FDA warning letter is a formal notice, not a court ruling. What the letters to peptide sellers say, what happens after one and how we show them.
- [Peptides for hair loss: what works and what is marketing](https://peptidechooser.com/learn/peptides-for-hair-loss-what-works/): Finasteride and minoxidil are the FDA-approved hair loss options. What copper peptide serums and injectable peptides have behind them, and what clinics charge.

## About the site (6 pages)

- [About Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/about/): Peptide Chooser is an independent site that compares peptide products and sellers for people in the United States.
- [How we rate peptide products and sellers | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/how-we-rate/): The five checks Peptide Chooser runs on every peptide seller (lab reports, FDA letters, company, legal pages, fresh prices) and how each goal page is built.
- [Contact | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/contact/): Email Peptide Chooser for corrections with a source, questions about a listing, press and partnerships. We cannot answer personal medical questions.
- [Affiliate and medical disclosure | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/disclosure/): How Peptide Chooser earns money through labeled paid links, why commissions never change a rating, and why nothing on the site is medical advice.
- [Privacy policy | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/privacy/): What information Peptide Chooser collects when you visit or email us, how long we keep it, your rights, and how to contact us about your data.
- [Mistakes we fixed | Peptide Chooser](https://peptidechooser.com/corrections/): Every factual error Peptide Chooser has corrected, with the date, what was wrong and what changed. Send corrections with a source and we list the fix here.
